transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Asha Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Nina Carter (Head of ML, VectorWorks), Rafael Gomez (Data Eng), Sofia Li (Infra), Dev (Research Eng)

Auto-summary (may be rough): Deep dive on embeddings and reranking. Discussed vector dimensionality (768/1536/3072), approximate nearest neighbor recall vs candidate set size, reranker cross-encoder cost, batching and latency tradeoffs, quantization options (int8/int4), KV cache applicability for reranking & generative pipelines, plus Dedicated vs Private/VPC constraints. Action items to run benchmarks and schedule on-prem pilot.

Transcript:
00:00 Asha (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll do a technical deep dive today focused on embeddings and reranking performance and cost, we have Marcus on the call from our SE team.
00:12 Marcus (Redwood SE): hey hi all, excited to dig in, quick agenda — vector dims and storage/cost, retrieval (ANN) + rerank flow, batching/throughput tradeoffs, quantization options, and private/VPC notes.
00:25 Nina (VectorWorks): sounds good, main goal for us is sub-100ms end-to-end for top-5 reranking in our user search, cost needs to be under X per 1k queries but we'll share exact numbers later.
00:38 Rafael (VectorWorks): and we have roughly 10M items, embeddings currently 1536 dims, stored in Pinecone, but recall is inconsistent on long tails, so we look at hybrid rerank.
00:50 Marcus: okay that helps — curious, do you pre-filter in the DB to a candidate set then run an expensive cross-encoder rerank, or do you do embedding cosine re-rank end-to-end?
01:05 Rafael: currently ANN -> top-100 then cross-encoder on our side (self-hosted). Cross-encoder is BERT-ish, pretty slow. We're evaluating moving some reranking into Redwood to get predictable latency.
01:18 Asha: note that we can host an embedding model and also host a smaller reranker model — two important cost pieces: retrieval cost (ANN index ops) and rerank cost (per candidate scoring).
01:30 Nina: can you quantify memory/cost implications of 1536 vs 768 vs 3072 dims? that's where we hit budget questions.
01:42 Marcus: yeah so rough rules: vector size scales memory linearly — 1536 dims at float32 is ~6KB per vector, at float16 half that, at 8-bit quantized embedding tables much smaller. For 10M vectors: 1536*4 bytes ~= 6.1KB * 10M ~= 61GB (float32). float16 ~30GB. Using int8/8-bit storage or product quantization can drop to single-digit GBs but impacts recall.
02:10 Rafael: those numbers are helpful — what about latency for a single embedding request from Redwood hosted model? we need per-query latency <30ms ideally for embedding generation.
02:22 Marcus: embedding model latency varies by model and batch. For a single request on a GPU it can be ~10-30ms depending on model size; with batching you can get much better throughput but added latency. For production we often recommend async batching with an SLO-aware bucket, and dedicate a small pool so that tail latency is stable.
02:40 Sofia: on the infra side, what about KV cache — does that help for reranking workloads? sounds more relevant to decoder LM caching.
02:50 Marcus: good point — KV cache is mainly for autoregressive/decoder models to avoid recomputing keys/values across long contexts. For embedding-only pipelines KV cache isn't used. For reranking if you use a cross-encoder (full sequence encode) there's not a beneficial KV cache per se, but if you move to a dual-encoder & late interaction model there are caching strategies for candidate encodes. Also we do candidate embedding caching: store the vector table and avoid recomputing item embeddings — that's standard.
03:20 Nina: ok so caching item embeddings is obvious, question is can Redwood serve cached vectors in a low-latency pathway or do we need external store?
03:30 Marcus: we can do both: common pattern is to keep the vector index (ANN) close to the serving tier — Dedicated pools allow co-locating ANN index and the inference runtime for minimal network hops. For Private/on-prem you'd colocate them in the same VPC/host. Redwood's runtime supports prefix/candidate caching optimizations for frequent items.
03:53 Rafael: how do we account for rerank cost — if we do top-100 candidates and run cross-encoder scoring that's 100 forward passes per query — huge. Is there a hybrid pattern?
04:05 Marcus: yes hybrid is typical: ANN -> top-N (e.g., 100) -> lightweight pre-ranker (cheap dot-product or small dual-encoder) to reduce to 5-10 -> cross-encoder rerank on that small set. The small pre-ranker can be a quantized model to save cost.
04:30 Nina: what's the latency tradeoff? say we need 100ms E2E budget for rerank, how to budget?
04:40 Marcus: example split: ANN retrieval ~5-20ms (depending on index & co-location), small dual-encoder pre-rank batch maybe ~10-30ms, cross-encoder on 5 items maybe 30-50ms — so you can hit under 100ms if you carefully size candidate counts and use fast models. Network hops matter, so Dedicated/VPC helps.
05:05 Dev (Customer): do you have numbers for different batch sizes? like batching at 8/32/128 for rerank scoring?
05:12 Marcus: yes — for GPU inference, throughput increases with batch size until memory/compute saturates. For a cross-encoder BERT-like model, batch 1 on GPU might be 25ms per example, batch 8 might amortize to ~6-8ms per example (so overall 50-60ms total), batch 32 further improves but adds queueing latency. Redwood's continuous batching helps by grouping requests across a short time window; you can set max wait to keep latency budget.
05:45 Rafael: what's continuous batching max wait typical? we need tail latency predictable — we can't have some queries wait 200ms to fill batch.
05:53 Marcus: typical max wait is 5-30ms in production — you tune it to your SLO. For interactive 100ms SLO, we'd keep max wait near 10ms. That means batch sizes vary but you still get batched kernel efficiency.
06:10 Nina: quantization — if we quantize the reranker to int8 or int4 how much accuracy do we lose?
06:17 Marcus: it depends on model and dataset. For many encoder models, int8 leads to negligible impact (<1-2% on downstream metrics). int4 can be larger impact but some 4-bit kernels (GPTQ-like) preserve a lot. We recommend running an eval: baseline (float16), int8, int4 and compute recall@k / MRR differences. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles based on your evals.
06:44 Sofia: network & KMS — if we go Private, can Redwood integrate with our HSM/KMS for key storage?
06:50 Asha: yes, Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs. For on-prem we can integrate with your internal KMS. We'll share security docs.
07:00 Rafael: for 10M vectors, candidate index memory for 1536 dims — cost of storage vs in-memory ANN like HNSW — any guidance?
07:10 Marcus: with HNSW you typically keep compressed vectors in RAM for fast recall; product quantization + disk-backed indices is possible for cost saving but increases latency. For ultra low-cost, vector DBs use PQ and SSD; for sub-100ms you likely need more RAM and Dedicated nodes. We can run benchmarks with your dataset to show tradeoffs.
07:35 Nina: what's the cost delta if we increase dims to 3072 to improve recall — is it linear?
07:40 Marcus: roughly linear in storage and memory for embeddings. Compute for similarity ops is also linear. So doubling dims doubles memory and roughly doubles per-query compute cost (unless you use approximate PQ that reduces compute). So better to test whether a higher-dim model meaningfully improves downstream metrics before committing.
08:00 Rafael: can Redwood run the rerank cross-encoder on CPU for lower cost?
08:06 Marcus: you can run small models on CPU (and Redwood supports CPU pools) but cross-encoders are typically much faster on GPU. For low throughput workloads, CPU may be cost-effective but may not meet latency SLOs.
08:20 Nina: how do we measure cost per 1k queries in a hybrid pipeline? do you have a simple calc?
08:30 Marcus: yes we typically compute: (embedding model cost per query) + (ANN lookup cost) + (pre-ranker cost * avg candidates) + (cross-encoder cost * avg candidates after pre-rank). We'll share a spreadsheet with per-model tokens/time/cost numbers so you can plug in candidate counts and get $/1k.
08:48 Asha: action — Marcus will run a baseline using a small cross-encoder and dual-encoder pre-rank on Redwood Dedicated test pool with synthetic vectors.
08:55 Rafael: we'll upload 100k synthetic vectors and give access.
09:00 Marcus: noted. Also quantization note — for embedding generation model, quantizing the weights is possible but may slightly degrade embedding quality; often we quantize reranker/pre-ranker first.
09:18 Dev: any gotchas with approximate nearest neighbor libraries (hnsw vs ivf/pq) and recall/latency?
09:25 Marcus: HNSW gives very good recall for many cases but memory heavy. IVFPQ scales well for disk-backed but needs careful tuning for nlist/nprobe. We'll help tune those parameters during the bench.
09:40 Sofia: on Private deployment latency — if we host on-prem, network overhead is minimal but ops burden for us increases; what's Redwood's recommended pattern?
09:48 Asha: for enterprises with strict residency or network constraints we recommend Private with dedicated control plane and customer KMS; Redwood supports an on-prem package with a managed deployment pattern. We'll provide a runbook.
10:05 Nina: can you share examples of customers who moved from Pinecone+self-host cross-encoder to Redwood Dedicated? what improvements did they see?
10:13 Asha: (mentions anonymized case) one customer reduced tail latency by ~40% and cut rerank cost by ~25% by moving pre-ranker to quantized dual-encoder and colocating index and inference.
10:25 Rafael: question about monitoring — how do we track quality regressions when changing quantization or dims?
10:33 Marcus: Redwood Optimize integrates evals — you can run your query set and measure MRR/recall automatically and set regression alerts. We also recommend keeping versioned prompt/eval sets.
10:48 Nina: ok next steps recap?
10:52 Asha: recap: We'll share benchmark template and pricing spreadsheet (Asha), Marcus will run a baseline Dedicated pool bench and share results, VectorWorks will upload sample vectors and query set, and we'll schedule on-prem pilot week of 2025-03-24.
11:08 Rafael: thanks everyone, appreciate the details.
11:12 Asha: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and docs.
11:18 meeting end
